Character: the flame-shaped figure is Sol, exactly the mascot in the reference images (the turnaround sheet shows his shape from every side; the strip of faces shows every eye shape he makes in this shot). Round, plump gumdrop body with a red outer layer, an orange middle layer and a broad cream inner flame for the face. At rest his face is plain smooth cream with exactly two small tall navy #1C2447 oval eyes set low and close together, solid dark with no whites or highlights, and nothing else on it: nothing is drawn above his eyes and nothing below them. His eyes change ONLY as the beats below say; copy his eyes from each source frame exactly, the same shape, size and place. Sol gives off no sparks, particles or smoke. His layers and face move together as one body with a small soft wobble that settles. He keeps the same size and the same place in the frame as in the source video. The small floating marks near him (music notes, an exclamation mark, a sweat drop, dots, a light bulb, a star, yellow dashes) appear ONLY in the frames where the source video shows them, in the same place and size, and vanish when the source stops showing them.

Scene: a small sunny bathroom, inside a white bathtub alcove. The tub floor is smooth glossy white. The walls of the alcove are pale aqua square tiles with white grout lines. Warm daylight with soft cool shadows, so the room has depth and glow. On the far wall are one silver shower head, one round window glowing with warm cream light, one small white shelf holding one coral bottle, one lilac bottle and one yellow rubber duck, and one silver lever tap; none of them ever moves or changes. The shower is running: blue water drops fall straight down from the shower head in a narrow spray and land in one round pale-blue puddle on the tub floor. Paint the drops as falling water, exactly where the source video shows them. Along the left side of the tub hangs ONE mustard-yellow shower curtain with soft vertical pleats and a pale cream band along its bottom hem, on one silver rod with silver rings. CURTAIN RULE: it is the same single curtain in every frame, the same colour, with the same pleats and the same cream hem; it bends and swings ONLY as the source video shows and never tears, opens, wraps around Sol or changes length. The small pale blue-white clumps floating in the air are little puffs of steam. Paint each one as a small soft round puff of pale steam, the same size, in the same place and moving along the same path as in the source video, in every frame. STEAM RULE: add no other steam, fog, mist or cloud anywhere, and never let the puffs spread into a haze. 

Beats: 1. The shot opens behind Sol's shoulder: he stands in the lower left, facing the camera. From 0.15 to 0.7 seconds he turns round to face the shower, so we see his plain red-orange back, and then tips a little to one side. 2. CAMERA MOVE: from 0.8 to 1.5 seconds the camera rushes forward past him and up to the shower head; from 1.6 to 4.2 seconds it sinks straight down beside the falling water, all the way to the tub floor, exactly as in the source video. 3. The steam puffs near the spray travel DOWN beside the falling drops and, at the bottom, slide away from the spray along the tub floor, toward the camera. 4. The shot ends low, looking at the puddle where the water lands, with a few puffs sliding across the white floor. Sol's eyes are two navy ovals whenever his face is seen. ARM RULE: his arm nubs stay the same short stubs in every frame; he never reaches for or holds anything.
